gaps.title: A canvas that animates unprompted is not followed
gaps.noPage: reader-initiated animation is pinned by test/canvas_test.go; the unprompted case is the canvasStreamEvery knob, a configuration choice rather than a parity property

gaps.title: Icon fonts ship whole, never subsetted
gaps.noPage: a byte-cost gap, not a rendering one: whether the glyphs draw at all is fonts/icon-ligature's business
gaps.notes: fixed: a family refused at the transcoder's cap is cut down to the icons the page actually draws rather than dropped. The agent reads the ligature names off the markup that draws them and appends them to the @font-face rule as a -sky-icons descriptor (a descriptor and not a --custom-property, because stripUnusedVars removes custom properties nothing reads one pass earlier); SubsetFont drops the variable tables — gvar alone is 87% of Google Symbols — and blanks the outlines of every glyph no named ligature reaches, keeping glyph ids where they are so GSUB, cmap and hmtx cross unrewritten. 4,888,276 bytes of woff2 becomes 283,012 bytes of sfnt for a Chat toolbar's fourteen icons. fontKey hashes the address with the sorted names, so the pipeline's existing cache cuts each subset once and a page that has since found another icon misses on a different key. CFF outlines, contextual ligatures and non-default weights still refuse, and refusing is what every font over the cap did before

gaps.title: A font registered through the FontFace API cannot ship; its glyphs render as their ligature names
gaps.notes: measured to the wall: an API face finishes loading as a paramless CSS.fontsUpdated (a CSS-declared face's event names family and src), JavaScript cannot read a FontFace's source back out of it, and the agent's isolated world does not enumerate page-realm FontFaceSet entries at all — its document.fonts sees only CSS-connected faces. What remains is reading the page's own world, which the page could detect, and the mirror's first principle is that the page never knows. The investigation still shipped one thing: CSS.fontsUpdated now feeds __skyhook.fontFaceSeen, which synthesizes a @font-face for a family whose declaring stylesheet the agent cannot read — a CDN sheet's icon font ships even when sheet recovery failed

gaps.title: wheel and hover are protocol surface no client sends
gaps.notes: fixed for the widgets that consume the wheel themselves, which is the half that was wrong: a wheel turned over a gesture-claiming surface (the drag census: touch-action none, grab/resize cursors, role=slider, canvas regions) is taken from the browser, its ticks coalesced for a beat, and sent as one InWheel naming the node and where in its box the cursor sat, replayed landside with the pointer parked at that point first — cursor-anchored zoom zooms about the cursor. A wheel anywhere else deliberately stays the reader's own scroll, reported as scroll telemetry, exactly as before: streaming wheel deltas for documents would spend the link on what position telemetry already carries. widgets/wheel-zoom pins the widget half; the hover half of the old title is P-111's story

gaps.title: Password and sensitive-autocomplete values never cross the wire
The landside browser is a phone with a mouse: touch is never emulated, so maxTouchPoints is 0 and pointer-aware pages lay out differently per half
gaps.notes: fixed, the way the old known-gaps note said it would have to be: emulation arriving together with touch input to feed it. The client's viewport carries a touch flag read off navigator.maxTouchPoints; SetViewport turns on Emulation.setTouchEmulationEnabled landside when it is set; and every click and drag frame carries the pointer kind that made it (InputEvent.PT), so a finger's tap replays as Input.dispatchTouchEvent and its drag as the touch stream a page listening for pointerType 'touch' expects. touch/drag-pan pins all three layers: the pan arriving, arriving as touch, and the page seeing maxTouchPoints > 0. A right-click or double-tap still replays as the mouse idea it is; a drag onto a draggable source keeps the mouse-interception path that preserves the browser's own drag-and-drop; and a finger's drag onto a surface that never claimed touch-action replays as mouse — a page that never claimed the gesture is one touch moves never reach on a real phone, and its mouse-listening map hears the replay it was always listening for

gaps.title: File upload is not implemented
gaps.notes: the chooser is intercepted instead of shown: Page.setInterceptFileChooserDialog suppresses the landside dialog (headless never had one) and the ask crosses as TypeFileAsk naming the mirrored input; the mirror's own picker is suppressed too, since it opened into a document whose value can never cross. The reader answers with the shell's native picker — the click's activation usually survives the round trip, and the toast's Choose button is a fresh gesture when it does not — with a confirm past 5 MB. Files stream back as TypeUploadPart chunks on bulk through an ordered queue, land under one staging subdirectory per file so the page sees the reader's own filename, and DOM.setFileInputFiles fires the change the page was waiting for; a dismissed picker shows the page a dismissed chooser, and the staging dies with the tab or the kill switch. Pinned by TestAFileReachesThePagesChooser and TestPWAPickedFileReachesThePage, both asserting on the page reading the file's own bytes

gaps.title: Clipboard copy executes plane-side only; cross-tab paste fidelity is absent
gaps.notes: the copy leg is relayed, input-caused only: Browser.grantPermissions gives every origin the async clipboard (headless has no prompt, so ungranted meant every page Copy button rejected outright), and after replaying a click or key the agent's clipProbe reads the clipboard once and answers only with a change — seeded before it will relay anything, so whatever predates the document never crosses; nothing polls. The text travels as TypeClipboard (64 kB cap, Cause naming the input) and the shell writes it through the browser's own API inside the click's activation window, falling back to a toast whose Copy button is its own activation. Paste already worked: InText/InPaste carry the reader's text into the landside document. Chrome UI is invisible to the mirror probes, so the pins are TestACopyThePageMakesReachesTheReader and TestPWARelayedCopyLandsOnTheClipboard

gaps.title: Find-in-page has no chrome-UI affordance
gaps.noPage: a chrome-UI gap, not a mirror-rendering one

gaps.title: A frame is only preemptible between messages; a large snapshot owns the link while it sends
gaps.noPage: a latency property of the scheduler, measured by the netem suite's timings rather than by parity

gaps.title: The document is delivered whole, never viewport-first
gaps.noPage: a delivery-order property; parity measures the settled document, which is identical either way

gaps.title: A closed shadow root is invisible: such a component mirrors as its light DOM only
gaps.notes: closed means closed to the isolated world too: attachShadow's return value is the only handle, and it was handed to page script the mirror never sees. The two routes in are wrapping attachShadow before page scripts run — a main-world modification the page can detect, against the mirror's first principle — or serialising through the CDP DOM domain's pierce, which is a second, parallel serialiser for one corpus page. Both stand rejected for now; shadow/closed's geometry expectedFail pins the shape

gaps.title: Reader-preference media features are answered plane-side, so the two halves may genuinely lay out differently
prefers-color-scheme is settled landside; changing it re-snapshots every tab
srcset and sizes are dropped; one server-chosen rendition ships
An animated GIF ships its first frame only
Canvas, WebGL and video are photographs: region shots, taken after input, never live
Ad and creative networks are blocked landside, so their content never exists to mirror
Alerts, confirms and prompts are auto-accepted landside and never shown to the reader
gaps.notes: deliberate today, but confirm() answering yes to everything deserves a reader-visible affordance eventually

gaps.title: Landside scroll is matched by range fraction, so IntersectionObserver-driven lazy loading fires approximately
gaps.notes: document scrolls are now anchored, not proportional: the client names the mirrored element at its viewport top and where its box sits (ScrollEvent.Anchor/AnchorY), and the landside replay puts the same element at the same offset — exact even when the two documents differ in height, which substituted fonts alone guarantee on real pages. The range fraction remains as the fallback for an anchor a mutation has since removed, and still owns the at-the-bottom case. textmisc/scroll-lazyload pins the whole path: telemetry, anchor resolution, landside scroll, the page's IntersectionObserver firing, and the revealed text mirroring back

gaps.title: A mirrored sub-document is laid out plane-side against a box, not a viewport: reader fonts, no percentage heights, fixed and sticky resolve against the wrong thing
gaps.notes: three pieces make the stand-in behave like the viewport it replaces: layout containment on it re-homes absolute and fixed descendants that used to anchor to the bottom of the whole mirror; the shadow root's base sheet carries the sub-document twin of the margin-collapse padding (the shell's own stylesheet cannot reach past the boundary, which is why the top-document fix never applied inside frames); and data-sky-box is applied as the border box it was measured as, where content-box sizing added the stand-in's own border on top and ran every framed document 2px wide. The percentage-height chain itself already resolved — the stand-in's definite box is what 100% finds. frames/viewport-units pins all of it at zero nodes off

gaps.title: A cross-origin frame that cannot be mirrored stays a labelled box; past the depth or count limits, so does one that could be
A cross-origin frame smaller than 64x32 gets no label at all — indistinguishable from a bug
gaps.noPage: settled as the design: a frame below the label floor is an ad pixel or a tracking beacon, and naming its host would put furniture on every page that carries them. The affordance floor is FRAME_LABEL_MIN_W/H in agent.js; the frame element, its box and its src still cross, so a bundle can always tell the box from a bug

gaps.title: A select change never reaches the landside page except through a form submit
gaps.notes: fixed two-sided: the host sends a change event's selection as a setvalue (multiple selects join their values with newlines, the way submit serializes them), and the agent's setValue grew a SELECT branch that picks options through the native value setter and fires input+change. forms/select's interaction and attributes dimensions pin it

gaps.title: setvalue and blur are dispatched to the top-level agent only; a non-append edit inside a mirrored cross-origin frame is silently lost
gaps.notes: three fixes, one per leg: setvalue and blur route through evalInSlot like every other input; typed text is spliced by the frame's own agent (__skyhook.insertText) because Input.insertText only reaches the browser's focused frame, which a programmatic focus inside an inlined frame never is; and the host hands the echo the composed event target, since an input event from a sub-document's shadow root reaches the document renamed to the frame's stand-in. forms/frame-editing pins all three

gaps.title: A blob: image source serialises as a landside blob URL the client can never fetch: a broken image with no fallback and no Missing notice
gaps.notes: a blob image is described and shipped like any other; the bytes are read by an in-page fetch (Tab.fetchBlob) because only the page's own realm can resolve the URL the network stack has never heard of. A blob a frame minted, or one the page revoked before the pipeline asked, still fails — to the Missing notice now, not to a silent broken image. images/blob-src pins the working case

gaps.title: Favicons never travel: TabState.FaviconID is decoded by the client and set by nothing
gaps.notes: fixed in the same commit as P-109 (the chrome the page never carries): the agent names the page's icon — the smallest declared raster, or the /favicon.ico every browser would have asked for — the server fetches it landside, sniffs the magic bytes, and ships it inside TabState.FaviconID as a data URL; the strip seats it where the spinner goes. Chrome UI stays invisible to the mirror probes, so the pin is TestTheTabStateCarriesTheFavicon rather than a corpus page. The registry flip was missed in that commit and corrected after

gaps.title: HTML comments are never mirrored, though KindComment exists on both halves of the protocol
gaps.notes: renders nothing, so nothing is lost; kept as the record that the protocol claims surface neither end implements

gaps.title: object, embed and applet are dropped whole with no stand-in: an unexplained hole where an iframe gets a labelled box
gaps.notes: plugin containers now cross on the iframe bargain: the element (not its fallback children), its measured box, its computed display — the CSS that made it a block selects a tag the stand-in no longer answers to — and a host label when the box is big enough to owe one. textmisc/object-embed's geometry pins the healed hole

gaps.title: Dead wire surface: frames and fields declared on both halves and written by neither
gaps.noPage: wire bookkeeping with no rendering consequence; recorded so the next protocol change deletes it rather than trips over it
gaps.notes: deleted, at the moment the entry was recorded for: the next protocol change. TypeIntegrity (the divergence check is a fenced landside checkpoint answered by the hash already on every Ack, so it costs no frame), OpImage and Op.Image (an image binds through its node's attributes and its own frame), Op.Drop (the style path is append-only; removing a rule from a constructed stylesheet is real design work, not a field), ScrollEvent.Seq and ScrollEvent.Visible (telemetry is latest-wins and needs no sequence; image priority is decided landside from the position the frame already carries), and the 'select' input kind (selection is native in the mirror and the handler did nothing). Every number stays retired with a tombstone rather than reused, the way frame type 23 and InputEvent field 15 already were. The conformance fixtures did not move by a byte, which is the proof that nothing ever wrote any of it

gaps.title: Downloads are unhandled: a download link writes a file onto the VPS and the reader sees nothing happen
gaps.notes: a download now lands on the server first — Browser.setDownloadBehavior allowAndName into a directory of its own, each file named by GUID — and every state change is announced to every session as TypeDownload: the shelf belongs to the user, not a tab. The bytes cross the link only on an explicit, size-labelled ask (TypeDownloadCmd fetch), chunked as TypeDownloadPart on bulk where they cannot head-of-line-block a page, resumable from any offset, stoppable mid-flight; discard deletes the landside copy and the kill switch wipes the directory. The client toasts the landing, prices the fetch, and holds the file in a Transfers panel until saved. Chrome UI is invisible to the mirror probes, so the pins are e2e: TestDownloadsLandAndCrossOnAsk (protocol, both legs, second device, resume, refusal, discard) and TestPWADownloadArrivesOnAsk (the real client end to end)

gaps.title: window.open and a plain click on target=_blank open a landside tab no client tab will ever show
gaps.notes: popups are recognised at browser level by their opener — a page session's autoAttach never delivers them — and adopted as ordinary tabs (Browser.OnPopup, Session.PopupOpened): attach, mirror, announce, and snapshot the document if it settled before the agent existed (Tab.Adopted). Discovery can announce one target twice, so adoption dedups on the owned set. The reader is not switched to the new tab; a row appearing is the honest version of a window opening off-stage. nav/target-blank's shell-tab count pins it

gaps.title: There is no print path: window.print does nothing for the reader
gaps.notes: the page menu's Print entry prints the mirror with the reader's own dialog: the mirror is a complete local copy, print stylesheets included, so it costs no round trip and lands on a printer the reader can actually reach, which the landside browser's never was. The frame's sandbox gains allow-modals for exactly this call — nothing inside can open a modal without script, and allow-scripts stays off; the client's sandbox conformance test pins both directions. Residue, named here so it is not rediscovered: a page calling window.print() landside is invisible — CDP has no event for it — so page-initiated print still does nothing for the reader. Pinned by TestPWAWidgetChromeAffordances

gaps.title: mousemove-driven widgets — drag-and-drop, sliders, hover menus — have no input path
gaps.notes: closed in two waves, all through the real client. Drags: the census reads the affordances the page itself declared (grab/resize cursors, touch-action none, role=slider — legible plane-side because the mirror carries the page's CSS), the frame names both ends of the gesture (Node2/Point2), the replay pins the drop to the destination's landside box, and the browser's own drag-and-drop crosses via its dragstart/dragover/drop plane-side and Input.setInterceptDrags landside. Hover: a pointer resting 400 ms on a new element is a gesture — the one every hover menu is built on — and sends the InHover that parks the landside pointer where CSS :hover and JS mouseover see it, no streaming, at most one frame per rest. Sliders and native pickers were already served by setvalue-on-change. Pinned by widgets/drag-sortable, widgets/dnd-html5, widgets/slider-track, widgets/hover-menu, the drag_test.go suite and TestSlidersAndHoverMenusReachThePage

gaps.title: An audio element is photographed as a still control strip; no audio ever crosses
gaps.notes: deliberately deferred out of the product-feature round: real audio over a 250 kbps shared link is a transport project (an Opus side-channel with its own budget and preemption), not a gap fix, and the UXR consult ranked it below downloads, clipboard, upload, pointer widgets and print — every one of which loses reader data or intent today, where audio degrades to the still control strip the design already draws

gaps.title: DPR is never applied to image transcodes or region shots: every picture is soft on a 2x or 3x screen
gaps.notes: the transcode ceiling is now in device pixels: the landside tab emulates the reader's deviceScaleFactor, so the agent's devicePixelRatio is theirs, and describeImage scales the target by it (capped 3x) — folding the density into the dimensions folds it into the cache key, so readers at different densities never collide on one rendition. Region shots were already at density for the same reason: the capture renders under the emulated scale. fit() still never upscales past the source, so 1x sources cost nothing new. Pinned by TestPicturesShipAtTheReadersDensity, which opens the same page at densities 1 and 2 and measures what arrives; the parity runner still has no dpr-2 knob, so the e2e pin is the measurement

gaps.title: A prefers-color-scheme media query nested inside a plain style rule crosses with its question intact instead of being resolved landside
gaps.notes: fixed: a style rule's own text now takes the same three passes a block shipped whole gets (shippedWhole in collectRules case 1), so a media query nested inside it is answered landside like its top-level twin; css/nesting-scheme's assertion pins it

gaps.title: The shell's font-src 'self' may refuse every blob: webfont the pipeline ships
gaps.notes: fixed: font-src gains blob:, for the same reason img-src always had it — the client rebuilds @font-face sources from bytes fetched over the protocol, and 'self' alone refused every one of them at render. fonts/faces pins it: cspViolations 1 → 0 and skyprobe now loads plane-side; the page's remaining expected failure is P-003's apiface

gaps.title: An external SVG sprite reference resolves to a URL the sandboxed frame can never fetch: the icon renders as nothing
gaps.notes: the agent fetches the sprite from inside the page — browsers require these references to be same-origin, so it always can — carries the referenced fragment on the use element (data-sky-sprite, capped at 64KB) and re-points the reference at an id of the mirror's own; the patcher scrubs the fragment of script and foreignObject and builds it into a sprite holder on the frame's root, where a resync's body swap cannot take it. images/svg-sprite pins the materialized symbol, and its corpus page now serves the sprite same-origin the way the real pattern does — the old cross-origin reference drew nothing on either half, which is why every probe used to pass over a missing icon

gaps.title: A style write onto a canvas permanently blanks its photograph until the reader touches something
gaps.notes: the audit read the comment in host.ts restyled() — 'for a canvas it is permanent' — and the measurement says otherwise: restyled() re-hangs the photograph from the held blob, and media/canvas-restyle pins that it stays painted across a style write. The comment describes only the case where the bytes never arrived; it is the stale half of this record

gaps.title: The GIF tap-to-play the transcoder's comment promises does not exist in the client
gaps.notes: the promise is now kept: the still's metadata says it was made from an animation (ImageMeta.Anim, detected by decoding the whole GIF), the context menu over such an image offers Play animation with its cost named, and the want travels as the still's key plus @anim on the ordinary want list — so the cross-flight cache holds originals exactly the way it holds renditions. The pipeline answers from the URL it remembered at transcode time and ships the fetched bytes untranscoded after sniffing them as an image; the browser plays the GIF natively. Pinned by TestATapFetchesTheOriginalAnimation

gaps.title: The mirror's own :root color and font leak into pages that rely on UA defaults
gaps.notes: fixed twice over, once in each direction: the server re-points the page's html, body and :root selectors at the data-sky-doc stamp the patcher writes on mirrored roots (rewriteRootSelectors, css.go), so page rules stop styling the frame's own elements and pouring inherited colour into the mirrored chain; and the frame's boot styles no longer set inheritable properties on its root, so the shell's chrome stops leaking downward. The agent's synthesized canvas-ground rule keeps a marker (:root[data-sky-ground]) the rewrite passes through, and the frame supplies the html,body height:100% chain deliberately that the double-match used to supply by accident. css/ua-defaults pins both directions

gaps.title: A top margin that collapses through the page's body is lost at the mirror boundary
gaps.notes: fixed: a twentieth of a pixel of padding on the mirrored html (the frame's boot styles) blocks parent-child margin collapse at exactly the boundary the real document root blocks it, so a child margin collapsing through body offsets content inside the mirrored root instead of escaping into the frame and vanishing. Rounds to zero in every probe; css/margin-collapse pins it

gaps.title: The server's echo of the reader's own focus arrives a round trip late and yanks focus back into the field they have already left
gaps.notes: the host now stamps every focus-moving input with its sequence number and each mutation carries the input that caused it, so onFocus drops a focus echo whose cause predates the last focus-moving input (host.ts applyingCause < lastFocusInputSeq): the confirmation of a field the reader already left arrives, is recognised as stale, and moves nothing.
gaps.noPage: timing-dependent by nature: the executor settles before each step so every other page measures its own gap; the guard is exercised by every interaction page's focus traffic and the fix is pinned by the staleness comparison itself

gaps.title: Top-layer state does not cross: a popover the page showed, or a modal dialog, is closed in the mirror
gaps.notes: the agent reports top-layer membership as data-sky-open — read at serialisation and kept current by capture-phase toggle/close listeners, since the events do not bubble — and the patcher reproduces it with showPopover()/showModal() in the mirror's own document, whose top layer is the frame's. textmisc/disclosure's style dimension pins the shown popover

gaps.title: In the script-disabled mirror a canvas is not a replaced element: it stretches to its container and its attribute aspect ratio scales it
gaps.notes: the patcher restates the landside intrinsic size (width/height attributes, spec defaults 300x150 absent them) as inline custom properties, and the shell's zero-specificity :where(canvas) rule renders them — so the page's own CSS still overrides the size exactly as it overrides a real canvas's intrinsic one. media/canvas and media/canvas-restyle geometry pin it

gaps.title: The document hash disagrees across languages on non-ASCII text: the agent and patcher fold UTF-16 code units while the Go replicas fold byte-indexed runes, so a healthy mirror of any page with a multi-byte character in a text node's first 32 characters reports divergence
gaps.notes: fixed: Model.Hash folds UTF-16 code units exactly as the agent and patcher do (foldHashValue, model.go). No corpus page can measure this — the browser-to-browser suite compares two JavaScript folds that always agreed — so the pin is the shared cross-language vector: TestHashMatchesTheJavaScriptConvention (internal/mirror) and the patcher's 'folds the cross-language vector' case assert the same 1767627470 over the same nodes, covering an nbsp, an em dash, a surrogate pair and clipPath's case. Discovery evidence: capture 20260820-072612 of the Hacker News front page, where both recorded hashes reproduced exactly under the two conventions

gaps.title: The mirror renders every page in standards mode: a quirks-mode page loses its quirks — table cells stop refusing the page font, and the geometry cascade follows
gaps.notes: the snapshot now carries the landside parser's verdict (Snapshot.quirks — document.compatMode, not doctype presence, because an archaic doctype still parses into quirks), and the host re-opens the mirror's document without the doctype when it differs: compatMode is fixed at parse, so the rebuild is the mechanism, and it rewires everything the open wiped. real/hn-front's style dimension — 53 differing nodes, every table cell's font — pins the fix at zero. The one residue is catalogued as P-130. A frame whose mode differs from its top document's still renders in the top document's mode: one plane document has one parser

gaps.title: A shorthand property set with var() loses its longhands in used-CSS extraction: the CSSOM serialises them as empty strings, the wire carries “border-top-color: ;”, and the mirror's parser drops the declarations
gaps.notes: fixed: when a rule's cssText carries the empty-declaration signature, the agent heals it from the sheet's authored source text — a <style>'s text synchronously, a linked sheet's via an in-page fetch prefetched at startup — locating the rule by normalised selector and ordinal and believing the candidate only if it reproduces every declaration the broken serialisation still carried (healedRuleText, agent.js). css/var-shorthand pins the heal; the wikipedia page's figure borders were the discovering case

gaps.title: The isolated-world injection race can leave a navigated tab unmirrored: when ensureWorld loses to a navigation and the settle-time retries lose too, the mirror keeps a three-node about:blank document while the page renders fully landside
gaps.notes: hardened in three places, because the race has three ways to stick: an injection that fails no longer leaves its context id stored (forgetWorld — a world without its agent answered "__skyhook is not defined" for ever); the navigation and load paths retry world setup with spaced attempts abandoned when the page moves on (ensureWorldRetry); and eval itself rebuilds once when Chromium says the context is gone (deadContext), because createIsolatedWorld can bind the document being replaced and the stored id dies with it — the rebuilt world binds the document that is actually there, and the fresh agent snapshots itself on arrival
gaps.noPage: a CDP timing race, not reproducible by a corpus page on demand. Evidence from the thirty-article conformance sweep: bundle 00 (expectedNodes 3, agent.json started:false against a fully rendered page.html) and bundle 16 (the re-injected agent answers an empty fingerprint and serverHash 2166136261 — the bare FNV basis — while the 2068-node document it sent earlier renders plane-side); seven 'isolated world setup failed' warnings in one hour of local captures, most of which recovered on a later retry

gaps.title: The three fingerprint writers disagree at the edges: DOM nodeType against protocol kind for container roots, lowercased names against clipPath, 32 UTF-16 units against 32 runes
gaps.notes: fixed: the writers now share one vocabulary — protocol kinds (the agent maps a sub-frame document to the wire's fragment kind), ASCII-lowercased element names (unifying also the patcher's docHash, which had folded wire-case clipPath and would have disagreed with a healthy agent), and values cut at 32 UTF-16 code units, backing off a split surrogate pair (fingerprintWindow in agent.js and patcher.ts, HashValueWindow in model.go, modelFingerprint in the Go client). bundle triage keeps its tolerant comparator for bundles written before the fix

gaps.title: A collapsed-border table sizes its caption differently when its borders arrive after first layout: the mirrored figure runs 2px wide and a paragraph wrapping around the float re-wraps
gaps.notes: exposed by P-126's heal on real/wikipedia-article: with the caption borders restored, the mirrored thumbnail figure measures 262px against 260 landside — under every probed computed property agreeing, border-collapse and display:table included — and the two-pixel float difference re-wraps the lead paragraph, shifting 17 inline boxes by up to 135px. A fully static render of the same computed inputs measures identically in both nested and top-level contexts, so the leading suspect is Chromium's incremental table relayout when borders and image blobs arrive after the first pass — the same page settled to landside-equal coordinates when the heal arrived late rather than early. Deterministic across runs; the wikipedia page's geometry expectedFail pins the shape

gaps.title: A quirks-mode body stretches to the viewport minus its own margins landside; the mirrored body is an inner box, and CSS cannot state a margin-box stretch for it
gaps.notes: the residue of P-125's fix: with the mirror re-parsed into quirks mode, the mirrored html restates the root's viewport stretch with min-height:100%, but the body's version of the same quirk subtracts its own margins — 709px inside a 725px viewport with default 8px margins — and no static rule can say "fill your parent's content box minus your own margin box" for an ordinary block. A percentage min-height on the body resolves to the full 100% in quirks and overshoots by exactly the margins. real/hn-front's geometry expectedFail pins the single-node shape; every content row inside the body measures landside-equal

gaps.title: A tab's cached history flags described the page it had left: the back gesture at the start of a history was answered by the shell and vanished
gaps.notes: canBack/canForward are read with Page.getNavigationHistory and cached, and the cache described the previous page — not for a moment but until the next navigation asked again. Two mechanisms: a navigation's tail (the load event, the settle, a refresh) goes on asking about the page the reader has left and its answer lands last, and the browser announces a commit before its own history records it — a tab that had just committed the index answered with a single entry, about:blank. A tab at the start of its history still saying a page was behind it made the shell answer the reader's back gesture instead of letting it through, leaving the skyhook:here sentinel unarmed with nothing to say the gesture was heard. Fixed by stamping each read with the nav epoch it was asked under and dropping an answer a commit has overtaken (applyHistory), and by re-asking while the browser's current entry still names a page the tab is not on (historyDescribes, five tries 20ms apart, all landside). An earlier fix that blanked the flags for any frame it could not vouch for was wrong in the other direction and broke the ordinary back gesture; both directions being wrong is what says the choice was never between them. Pinned by TestAHistoryAnswerTheReaderNavigatedPastIsDropped and TestAHistoryReadIsCheckedAgainstThePageTheTabIsOn; the failure it explains is TestTheBrowsersOwnBackAndForwardDriveTheTab over the emulated link

gaps.title: A message the page never sent was drawn as sent, and the next one was typed into a composer that still held it
gaps.notes: two of a reader's Google Chat messages arrived as one bubble — "the icons are still missing :/" and "message" — because Chat's emoji autocomplete kept the Enter for itself, turning `:/` into U+1FAE4 and sending nothing (the landside capture shows the emoji in the bubble, and the server fetched notoemoji/1fae4 0.57s after the Enter). Three things of ours made that silent. The echo engine clears the composer and draws an optimistic ghost on Enter with no failure path, so a send that never happened left a bubble reading as sent for the rest of the session. The agent watched only INPUT, TEXTAREA and OPTION for a live value, and liveValue read el.value — undefined on a contenteditable — so the composer every modern chat app uses never reported its text, while the real DOM changes to it were deferred because the echo owns the subtree. And reconcileAttr read op.str, which is the field a *title* op carries and is empty on every attribute op ever sent, so nothing was ever reconciled for any field. Fixed: an editing host is watched like a field (bounded at LIVE_TEXT_MAX so a document editor does not ship its document), reconcileAttr resolves the value from the intern table and only for data-sky-value, an echo caused by an edit the reader has already typed past is ignored, and a composer that comes back non-empty after a ghosted send takes the ghost back. Pinned by TestAComposerReportsWhatThePageWroteIntoIt, TestADocumentSizedEditorIsNotReportedOnEveryChange, TestPWAAnOptimisticMessageIsTakenBackWhenThePageKeepsIt and three cases in client/test/host.dom.test.ts

gaps.title: A font the page inlines as a data: URI is refused by the shell's CSP: the ligature fires and the glyph draws nothing
gaps.notes: font-src was 'self' blob: — blob: for the faces the client rebuilds from protocol bytes (P-115) — and nothing for the ones a page inlines in its own stylesheet. An icon font is exactly the size that invites inlining: Google Chat ships the subset that draws its toolbar and its Starred shortcut as a data:font/ttf URI, nothing this side rewrites it, and it was refused as itself. Silent in the same way P-115 was — the face registers, the ligature fires, the glyph draws nothing — and a reader's capture counted 50 securitypolicyviolations while its own screenshot showed the icons, because capture.ts rasterises through an <svg><foreignObject> in the shell's document where the mirror frame's policy does not apply. Fixed by adding data: to font-src, as img-src has had all along

gaps.title: Scrolling a container plane-side never reached the page: a list that builds its rows on demand never built any more
gaps.notes: a reader scrolling Google Chat's emoji picker watched it show blank space. The picker builds the cells it needs and no more, so the mirror had the 112 that happened to exist and scrolling past them found nothing — and the server log has not one line for the twenty-five seconds of scrolling before the capture. Everything the answer needed was already built: ScrollEvent.Node, HandleScroll's container branch, the agent's scrollTo(id,x,y), and P-118's container positions in the snapshot. What was missing was at the plane-side end — onElementScroll noticed a container being scrolled, recorded that the reader had taken it over so a server scroll would not move them, and told the server nothing. The document's own scroll had been reported since the beginning; a container's never was, which made the landside branch dead surface in the same way wheel is. Fixed by reporting a scrolled container the way the document is reported, throttled per element on the same 250ms. Pinned by TestPWAScrollingAMirroredContainerReachesThePage, which fails without it, and by TestScrollingAContainerBuildsTheRowsBelowIt for the landside half that had never been reached; and a second half, which only the emulated link ever saw: the report was throttled by 250ms and read the box when the timer fired rather than when the reader scrolled. In that window the server's own position for the container — one from before the scroll, still in flight — arrives and is applied, because followScroll declines to move a scroller the reader has taken over except when they are at the bottom of it, which is exactly where a reader who has just scrolled to the end of a list is. The box went back, and the report then described that instead of the scroll. The position is taken as the reader leaves it now, and client/test/host.dom.test.ts pins the race deterministically rather than waiting for a shaped run to catch it; and a third time, the same window and the other half of it. The report named the node by looking it up when the timer fired, and a document the server replaces inside that window — a resync, a navigation — rebuilds the patcher's map, so the element the reader scrolled stops having an id and the report gave up without a word. Caught by instrumenting the two moments: id=8 at the scroll, id=0 a quarter of a second later, which is why the shaped job's log recorded nothing at all. The id is taken with the position now, at the moment the reader scrolls

gaps.title: A checkbox's third state never crossed: indeterminate is a property with no attribute, so a half-ticked box mirrored as empty
gaps.notes: found by audit rather than by a reader — the same shape as P-132's composer text, one control along. The agent watched INPUT/TEXTAREA value and checked and OPTION selected; indeterminate reflects no attribute at all, so a serializer that walks attributes sees a box that is merely unchecked. The pattern is the header tick of a partly-selected list — a mail app's message list, a file manager, any table with a select-all — and the reader was shown the wrong answer to the only question that box asks. It now travels as data-sky-indeterminate beside data-sky-checked, on all four surfaces that carry live state: the serializer, the sweep, the parity probe's read-only twin, and the patcher (including the removal path, since dropping the attribute has to unset the property). Pinned by TestAHalfTickedBoxCrossesAsHalfTicked

gaps.title: A failing e2e test's log dump was 93% Chromium's complaints about the machine, so the records describing the mirror had been pushed out of the ring
gaps.notes: a headless Chromium writes dozens of lines about the absent system bus and the absent GPU in its first second, on every machine this runs on, and drainStderr logged all of them at DEBUG. The diagnostic ring is 500 records shared with everything the mirror has to say, and in the e2e harness — where every test starts its own browser — the browser had taken it over: a failing test's dump came out 93% dbus, with ten records of mirror left in it. That is the first thing CLAUDE.md tells you to read when a test fails, and it had stopped being worth reading. The known-worthless lines are dropped at the drain now, matched on message rather than severity because the browser calls all of them ERROR and some real ones are ERROR too, and a read carrying several lines is split so a real line does not go out with the noise. The fix paid for itself immediately: with dbus gone, the dumps of the remaining local flakes are dominated by repeated TLS handshake failures, which is a lead rather than a wall. Pinned by TestTheBrowsersComplaintsAboutTheMachineAreNotLogged

gaps.title: A frame emitted between a commit and its history read moved the address bar onto the new page with the old page's back button
gaps.notes: the other end of P-131, and what was still failing after it. A commit moves the tab's URL at once — onFrameNavigated has the address the moment the browser announces it — and its history flags a round trip later, because Page.getNavigationHistory has to be asked. The commit's own frame waits for that answer and carries both, deliberately; but it is not the only thing emitting. The new page's snapshot arriving, its loading stopping, its favicon landing all call emitState, which filled a missing URL in from t.url and stamped every frame with the cached canBack — so any of them emitted inside that window shipped the new address with the previous page's history. Going back to the first page of a tab is where it bites, because about:blank stops loading in less time than one CDP round trip: the client was told "you are on about:blank" and "you can still go back" together, drew the empty address bar and the start page, and answered the reader's next back gesture instead of letting it through to the browser. P-131's retry loop widened the window rather than causing it — up to five 20ms waits before the flags land — which is why the unshaped job started failing where the shaped one had been fixed. Fixed by making a frame emitted in that window say nothing about where the tab is: the URL goes out empty, which the client reads as unchanged, and the flags beside it are the ones the client already holds, since the only thing that writes them is a read for the page the tab is on. The commit and the URL now move under one lock too — the window used to be a clipboard grant wider. Pinned by TestAFrameEmittedBeforeTheHistoryReadSaysNothingAboutWhereTheTabIs; the failure it explains is TestTheBrowsersOwnBackAndForwardDriveTheTab on the unshaped job, trap at skyhook:here with the tab reporting no page behind it

gaps.title: A verdict about an image erased the description of it: the alt text of an asset that 404s was lost to whichever frame landed last
gaps.notes: protocol.ImageMeta is two messages sharing a body. One describes an asset — size, type, blurhash, and the alt text of the element that referenced it — and comes from the snapshot that named it or the transcode that made it. The other is a verdict, {Hash, Missing: true}, sent from the four places in the pipeline that can conclude the bytes are not coming, none of which ever learned anything else about the key: only abandon() holds a Request, and only for the tab that asked. internal/client replaced its table entry for entry, so a verdict wiped the description — and answerIfStranded fires whenever a client's ImageWant reaches a key that is neither done nor in flight, which on the emulated link is any key the pipeline gave up on before the want arrived. TestAnImageThatCannotBeFetchedIsReportedRatherThanLeftPending asserts the alt travels, and failed on it on the shaped job. The mirror's own client never had this: it fills an element's alt in from the meta only when the element has none, because the alt it renders came with the element. Fixed by folding rather than replacing — a field the frame does not carry is left alone, with Missing the exception in both directions, since it is the whole of what a verdict says and a later description is the key's second chance. Pinned by TestAVerdictAboutAnImageKeepsWhatIsKnownAboutIt

gaps.title: A second finger is dropped where it lands: no multi-touch gesture has a path
gaps.notes: fixed: a second finger landing on a surface that claimed the whole gesture becomes the other half of it rather than being dropped. The two paths are sampled at the same instants — one frame per move of either finger — so the wire carries a gesture rather than two, and the landside replay walks both as touch points together (Path2, field 23). A pinch is measured by the change in the gap rather than by displacement, because a symmetric spread moves the midpoint nowhere and a displacement test would throw away the commonest pinch there is; it names no drop target, because what it did happened between the fingers. Pinned by touch/pinch-zoom, TestTwoFingersPinchThePage and host.dom. Two things the same work fixed: a second finger's moves used to feed the first finger's path, so a two-finger gesture sent one zigzag drag between them; and the drag sampler shared the approach path's spacing rule, which dropped a second finger's every move because the first had just been sampled

gaps.title: A widget that claimed one axis is not claimed at all: touch-action pan-x/pan-y goes unread
gaps.notes: fixed: the census reads what a touch-action value leaves to the browser and claims the rest — pan-y keeps the horizontal gesture for the page, pan-x the vertical, none both, and manipulation (a faster tap, not a claim) neither. A drag is then only sent if it ran mostly along the claimed axis, because a gesture along the browser's axis is the browser's: under a finger it never arrives (the scroll claims it and the pointer cancels), under a mouse it is the reader scrolling or selecting. The wheel path checks the same axis, which is what keeps a carousel from swallowing the vertical scroll over it. widgets/swipe-carousel pins the horizontal claim; host.dom pins the vertical drag and the vertical wheel staying native

gaps.title: Page keyboard shortcuts never cross: only control keys are forwarded
gaps.notes: fixed on both halves. Plane-side: a printable key pressed with no field holding the caret goes landside as an InKey, which is what a page's own shortcuts are made of. Deliberately not forwarded — a key typed into a field (it belongs to the field and travels as text), a ctrl or meta chord (the browser's, except the two the shell claims, which are now offered to the shell because an event inside the frame never reaches the shell's document), anything with alt (the OS's), and the space bar, whose default action outside a field is to scroll the mirror natively and for free. Landside: a printable InKey is dispatched as the keystroke it was rather than inserted as text — Input.insertText fires no keydown and needs an editable to insert into, so a shortcut key did nothing at all. Auto-repeat is carried too: the client pools a held key's repeats into one frame with a count, which the replay has always honoured up to 32. Pinned by widgets/key-shortcuts, TestAPagesOwnKeysReachIt and host.dom

gaps.title: The echo engine held the server's focus echo and replayed it at blur, putting the caret back in the field the reader had just left
gaps.notes: found by widgets/key-shortcuts, whose click out of a text field kept landing back in it. The echo engine buffers server ops that touch the field the reader owns, so their rewrites do not fight the typing — but it buffered focus ops too, and replayed them on blur: the instant the reader leaves. That lands past both guards, because the host's staleness check reads the cause of the mutation being applied and a replayed op carries none, and its owned-field check has just been cleared by the blur itself. The caret jumped back into the field, and on a phone the keyboard with it. A focus op is about a moment rather than about content, so it is no longer deferred at all: it reaches the host, which ignores it while the reader owns the field, which is what it was for. The P-121 family's third instance — after the round-trip echo and the composer value

gaps.title: One un-deadlined CDP call wedged a tab's inbound queue for good, and nothing anywhere said so
gaps.noPage: a liveness gap in the inbound queue, not a rendering one: the mirror was a perfect copy throughout, and bundle triage says clean on every tab
gaps.notes: found in a Hacker News capture. Tab 1's last frame went out at 00:15:22; the reader then tapped one story's comments link three times over the next forty seconds, at 00:24:44, 00:24:59 and 00:25:25. All three are in the session timeline, which records an input on arrival, and none of them was replayed: no navigation, no tab-work failure, not one line in the server log, and the landside agent still reporting focusedId 59 — the story link focused by a click at 00:15:02. Per-tab queues had moved this wedge off the connection without bounding it, so a job ran with no deadline of any kind and cdp.Call blocks forever on a request the browser never answers. Everything else about the tab stayed alive, which is why it looked fine: the mirror matched the page, and the thirty-second integrity check passed twice between the taps. Fixed by giving each piece of inbound work a budget chosen by which side of the link its call is on — three minutes for a navigation, a page build or a resync, thirty seconds for a click, a scroll or an upload — and by saying so when one is abandoned: a WARN, a job-abandoned event in the session timeline, and running/queued/jobsAbandoned on the tab's page in a bundle, none of which existed to be read the first time

gaps.title: A cross-origin frame whose target dies without a detach event is asked to re-snapshot every two seconds for the life of the tab
gaps.noPage: needs a cross-origin frame whose CDP target dies mid-load and a top-level navigation over it; the corpus is hermetic and static by rule, so the shape has no page
gaps.notes: the same Hacker News capture, one layer down. An article opened four cross-origin frames; the m.stripe.network one lost its CDP session within the second, and the reader pressed back over it. No Target.detachedFromTarget ever arrived, so nothing marked the frame gone — and resplice, which resets every frame on each new top-level document, kept handing it back to the reconciler. It was asked to say itself again 330 times over ten and a half minutes, across three more navigations, on a page whose own agent reported zero frames. The retry pair was 664 of the 983 lines in the bundle's log, which is two days of history evicted to hold them, and DocHash walked it and failed, so the capture could not fingerprint the one tab the reader was complaining about. Fixed the way reconcile itself is argued for — check the state rather than trust the event: a refusal backs the frame off, doubling from one tick, and six refusals in a row retire it, freeing its slot and taking its subtree out of the client's document. DocHash now walks spliced frames only, the list Checkpoint already used, because a frame that was never spliced put no nodes in anyone's document
